Virtual echo: what this probe records
2D linear measurements following ASE 2019 comprehensive TTE guideline, Table 3 (Mitchell et al.), plus RV wall thickness from the ASE/EACVI 2015 chamber quantification guideline (Lang et al.). TEE rows use the views of the ASE/SCA 2013 comprehensive TEE guideline (Hahn et al.); their normal values are the TTE ranges, because these guidelines give no separate TEE ranges. Click a row to jump to its view and highlight that measurement.
ViewMeasurementHow the guideline measures itPhaseEdgesAtlasNormal

The atlas is a single end-diastolic shape. Measurements the guideline takes at another phase (LA diameter, LA and RA lengths at end-systole; aortic annulus and LVOT at mid-systole) are approximated at end-diastole and flagged. Not measurable here: LVIDs (systolic), LVOT diameter (the atlas mitral valve is a closed surface with no open anterior leaflet to measure to), and the IVC diameter (atlas IVC is a short stub). Normal values: LV, RV, RVOT and LA diameters are normal ranges from Lang 2015; aortic values are mean ± SD (orange if more than 2 SD away). Orange values are outside the normal range; for an average shape this is a property of the atlas, not a diagnosis.

Fan sector: 90° wide by default. The depth starts at the smallest whole centimetre that holds the chambers, valves and great arteries in that view, and never more than the 17 cm the earlier version used everywhere. Both can be changed with the sliders; a shallower depth enlarges the picture, as on a scanner. Measurements that fall outside the current sector are shown faded.

TEE views follow the ASE/SCA 2013 comprehensive TEE guideline (Hahn et al.). The oesophagus and stomach are drawn as simple tubes for orientation (the atlas does not include them). Upper-oesophageal aortic arch and descending aortic views are omitted because the atlas aorta stops before the arch. TEE measurements: RV length and diameters and mitral annulus (ME 4-chamber), mitral annulus (ME 2-chamber and ME long axis), aortic annulus and sinuses (ME AV long axis), tricuspid and pulmonary annulus (ME RV inflow–outflow), and septal wall, LV diameter and lateral wall (TG mid papillary short axis). The atlas valves are closed surfaces, so each annulus is the widest span of the valve surface in that plane. Sinotubular junction and ascending aorta are left out for TEE: in the ME AV long-axis plane the atlas aorta narrows steadily without a clear junction.

Ribcage (TTE only): bone cut from the MM-WHS 2017 cardiac CT (training case 1001, same scan as the CT explorer) where the CT number shows bone, and moved onto the atlas heart by matching the four chambers (scale 0.955; median surface distance 2.5–4.6 mm). Each voxel keeps its real CT number (Hounsfield units). In the echo, every scan line is followed from the probe: at the edge of bone part of the sound is reflected (bright line) from the impedance jump, and inside bone the rest is absorbed in proportion to bone density (density and speed of sound estimated from the CT number; from about 2.4 dB per mm for cancellous bone up to 12 dB per mm for dense cortex, assuming 2.5 MHz), so the region behind a rib turns dark. The scan has a tight field of view, so lateral ribs near the apex are partly missing, and costal cartilage is not calcified so it does not shadow. The atlas probe positions were not fitted to this chest; if a rib blocks the view, slide the probe to the next intercostal space. TEE beams do not cross the chest wall, so no rib shadow is drawn for TEE. MM-WHS data are covered by the challenge data agreement.

Heart: mean shape of the Rodero et al. (2021) statistical shape model (PLOS Comput Biol 17(4): e1008851). The echo is the atlas geometry sliced by the beam plane, not a physics simulation.
